title: PART 2 / SECRET INGREDIENTS
goal: Gather visual clues, read Chapter One, and use evidence to explore character choices behind the friendship conflict.
outcomes: Identify relevant details and make one inference from the clue scene.
Record important events, clues, and character choices from Chapter One.
Explain a character choice or conflict using story evidence.
focus: Look for observations and character inferences supported by evidence, rather than guesses alone.
assessment: Clue Hunt: students name a visible detail and support one quick inference. Chapter Notes or chosen Small Bite: students refer to a character action or event as evidence.

rows.description: Play the 3-minute scene. Students jot 2–3 visible clues in a notebook or on paper while it plays.

rows.text: Quickly share one observed clue. Distinguish what students saw from what they think it means.
What might be inside the CONFIDENTIAL envelope, and what clue supports that idea?

links.description: Full written tracker; +10–15 min. Use the drawing box to sketch an extra observed clue or unresolved detail.

rows.description: One per student; legacy guide p. 10.

rows.text: Before reading, students jot or sketch one prediction about Chapter One.
Choose one delivery: independent reading, partners/small groups, or a whole-class read-aloud. Listening is an alternative.

rows.description: Chapter One; open for the chosen reading format.

rows.text: As they read or listen, students record 2–3 important details: a clue, a character choice, or something that changes their prediction. Short notes or sketches are fine.

links.description: Chapter One audio folder; listening alternative

rows.text: Use the Conflict Report and Zenix Debrief prompts from the original lesson slides 17–18. Students discuss in pairs or small groups; a short written response is optional.
What hurt Maddie most about the team switch? What evidence supports that view?
Choose one character. In a notebook, record 2–3 known facts, one possible feeling or goal, what the character said or did as evidence, and one remaining question.
Which clue or character choice matters most so far, and what supports your thinking?

bonuses.description: — Optional +10–15 min: complete the full eight-question tracker. The drawing box is for sketching additional evidence.
— Optional +15–20 min: complete the expanded character profile, distinguishing evidence from imagined details.
